headline: Approved Comcast conduit on Sycamore Street and $2,082,498 bond for two fire trucks; referred short-term rental and backyard cottage zoning changes.
summary: Members approved a $2,082,498 bond for two fire trucks, several grants, and labor contract payments. They referred the Poplar Street pump station bond, a short-term rental ordinance change, and backyard cottage zoning petitions to committees. Resolutions on heat pump permits, school restrooms, and Head Start were also approved.

transcript:
# City of Somerville, Massachusetts · City Council · Meeting Minutes

Thursday, October 8, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:06 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered recess at 7:27 PM and returned at 7:35 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 9:04 PM and returned at 9:13 PM.

1.1. Roll Call

Call of the Roll.

## (ID # 26-1490 ) RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

- Present: Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen
- City Councilor At Large Jon Link
- Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott
- Ward Four City Councilor Jesse Clingan
- City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo
- Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait
- City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler
- Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt
- Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin
- City Councilor At Large Wilfred N. Mbah
- Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1491 )

- Councilor McLaughlin and the entire Council requested a moment of silence
- in memory of Theresa Hussey-Rogers.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Keith
- Michael Mannix.

## RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Regular Meeting of August 27, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1492 ) RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

2.1. Citation

By Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1481 ) Commending Nancy Paz for her work with Latino families in the community.

Discussed with items #26-1482, #26-1483, #26-1493, #26-1471.

- Councilor Ewen-Campen recognized each citation recipient, highlighting

their contributions and service to the Latino community. Each recipient expressed appreciation to the City Council for the recognition and its

- continued support of the city’s immigrant community.

## RESULT: APPROVED

2.2. Citation

By Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1482 ) Commending Alejandra Bañuelos for her work with Latino families in the community.

Discussed with items #26-1481, #26-1483, #26-1493, #26-1471

## RESULT: APPROVED

2.3. Citation

By Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1483 ) Commending Maritza Perdomo for her work with Latino families in the community.

Discussed with items #26-1481, #26-1482.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

3.1. Grant of Location Comcast applying for a Grant of Location to install 187 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1459 ) Sycamore Street and Broadway and one new sidewalk vault, from the existing Comcast Manhole at the intersection of Sycamore Street and Broadway, passing through the proposed sidewalk vault, continuing to points of pickup at 382 Broadway and 386 Broadway.

Dave Flewelling, representing Comcast, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed. Councilor Link noted that a curb cut is detailed in the plans and Mr. Flewelling replied that it would receive a temporary

- patch followed by a concrete restoration.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.2. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 346 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1456 ) Newton Street, from the existing Manhole 4115, passing through the existing Manhole 4123 to a point of pickup at existing Manhole 31223 next

- to 24 Webster Avenue.

Councilor Scott recused himself from consideration of the item.

- Michael Katz, an abutter, inquired whether Eversource would coordinate

work on a neighboring property to minimize disruptions in the area. He also requested clarification regarding the anticipated project schedule, duration of construction, and how abutters would maintain access to their homes and driveways throughout the project.

- No representative from Eversource was present to address the questions or

provide additional information. With no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Licenses and Permits Committee

3.3. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 15 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1457 ) Fellsway West Street, from existing Manhole 1897 to a point of pickup at

the demarcation line next to 49 Fellsway West.

- Emmy McSweeney, representing Eversource, informed the Council that
- Eversource would like to withdraw this item.

## RESULT: WITHDRAWN

3.4. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 266 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1458 ) School Street, from existing Manhole 29855, passing through existing

Manholes 13425 and 13085 to a point of pickup at 93 Highland Avenue.

Emmy McSweeney, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Ordinance

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1476 ) That Section 12-111.1 of the Code of Ordinances be amended as detailed

herein to protect private significant trees during construction.

Councilor Sait explained that, under this ordinance, tree protection would be extended to all significant trees on private property.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Legislative Matters Committee

4.2. Resolution

By Councilor Sait and Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1474 ) That the Director of Inspectional Services clarify the permitting process for

heat pump systems.

- Councilor Sait expressed concerns regarding the complexity of Somerville’s

permitting process and noted that certain requirements may be outdated. She reported having discussed these concerns with staff from the Inspectional

Services Department, who will review the existing process and identify opportunities for updates and improvements.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee

4.3. Resolution

By Councilor Sait, Councilor Link and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1475 ) That Chief of Police provide an update to this Council regarding the Municipal Road Safety Grant Program.

- Councilor Sait requested a detailed breakdown of how the grant funds are

allocated and expended prior to consideration of any future acceptance of the grant.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.4. Ordinance

By Councilor Link, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Ewen-Campen

(ID # 26-1501 ) That the Short-Term Rental Ordinance be amended as detailed within.

- Councilor Link explained that the proposed amendment to the ordinance is

intended to encourage the return of certain short-term rental properties to the long-term rental market while strengthening the City’s ability to enforce the ordinance.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Legislative Matters Committee

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Scott

(ID # 26-1498 ) That the Director of Mobility add more secure bicycle parking at the Argenziano School.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.6. Resolution

By Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1499 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works, in consideration of children with

sensory sensitivities, utilize electric leaf blowers when doing maintenance on school grounds during school hours.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee

4.7. Resolution

By Councilor Link and Councilor McLaughlin

(ID # 26-1500 ) In support of meeting spaces for Alcoholics Anonymous.

Councilor Link emphasized the importance of ensuring the availability of community meeting spaces. Councilor McLaughlin expressed concern

regarding the loss of meeting space at the Ralph and Jenny Center, noting that he had previously understood the space would remain available

following the City’s assumption of control of the property. He requested clarification regarding the City’s plans for the building.

- Director of Intergovernmental Affairs Amanda Nagim-Williams explained

that three groups had previously utilized the Ralph and Jenny Center for meetings, two of which have since been relocated to alternative spaces. She stated that the City has prioritized securing a suitable meeting location for the remaining group.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Public Health and Public Safety Committee

4.8. Resolution

By Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1467 ) That the Director of Planning submit a plain-language explanation and fact

sheet for each proposed zoning amendment, to be attached directly to the corresponding zoning amendment item.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.9. Resolution

By Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1493 ) Recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month and the contributions of Somerville’s

Hispanic, Latin American, and Caribbean communities.

Discussed with items #26-1481, #26-1482, #26-1483, #26-1471.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.10. Resolution

By Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-1468 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works repair all broken and inoperable

- plumbing, appliances and privacy treatments of the Winter Hill Innovation

School bathrooms and provide regular work timelines in writing, detailing when work will be initiated to when work is anticipated to be fully

- completed.

Discussed with item #26-1469.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee

4.11. Resolution

By Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-1469 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works immediately repair the urinal

- fixture, otherwise known as 'The Blaster', at the Winter Hill Innovation

School and present written updated work timelines on a regular basis until the urinal fixture is entirely repaired.

Discussed with item #26-1468.

Councilor Strezo read a letter from a fourth-grade student outlining several longstanding restroom maintenance issues that have reportedly remained

- unresolved for years.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

- Urging Governor Healey to end the Massachusetts Department of

- Councilor Hardt expressed concern regarding the number of detentions by

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), stating that detentions have reached an all-time high this year. She provided an overview of the federal 287(g) program, which allows participating state and local law

enforcement agencies to collaborate with ICE on immigration enforcement, including the transfer of certain incarcerated individuals to federal

- immigration custody upon completion of their sentences.

- Councilor Hardt sponsored Somerville resident and attorney Kristen Laselle
- to speak on the item. Ms. Laselle expressed concerns that ICE exploits
- 287(g) agreements in ways that create risks for local communities.

- Councilor Wheeler discussed the potential benefits of the PROTECT Act

and acknowledged ongoing discussions regarding 287(g) agreements. He noted differing perspectives among those involved in these discussions, with some advocating for the termination of such agreements and others

expressing concern that ending them could result in more adverse consequences.
